body:
Thank you for reporting.
Does it only happen with android project? And does it open happen with 0.4.5-rc2? Thanks.

I'm not sure, the only project I've used recently has android targets. It's 0.4.5-rc2 (from source, using the commit above). I've seen it only twice during the whole day today, so it's quite hard to reproduce.
Then it will be hard to fix.. @ahumesky Add android person in case he knows.
we've made a number of changes to the android_sdk_repository rule recently, adam can you take a look?

I'll take a look this week, but I suspect the culprit is in either 06072c557290b97cb2d2e4fd255b647a9208cb5c or 9d88394848fa6742513d85fa5f892ae1702d015e.

@damienmg Can you confirm that adding the dep on the ANDROID_HOME environment variable did not cause this?
@aj-michael I can confirm it is not 9d88394 but 06072c5 is the likely culprit. More precisely look at https://bazel-review.googlesource.com/c/8137/ which fix similar issues in AndroidNdkRepository.
@simonhorlick in the android_sdk_repository rule in your WORKSPACE file, are you setting the path attribute or not setting it (which should read from $ANDROID_HOME)?
I wasn't able to repro on the android tutorial, would love to have a good repro.
I thought I would be able to find a missing null check in 06072c5, but I have not found one. It would be nice if skyframe reported which dependency was null instead of just the GroupedListHelper.
Humm how can we request the directoryListing if we do not have the actionenvvariable resolved?
Ok I think I have the fix, that's stupid me did something incorrect.

https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/ed7795234ca7ccd2567007f2c502f853cd947e50/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/bazel/rules/android/AndroidSdkRepositoryFunction.java#L85 does not check for the return value (see the correct code here: https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/ed7795234ca7ccd2567007f2c502f853cd947e50/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/bazel/repository/skylark/SkylarkRepositoryFunction.java#L75)
Ooooh, nice catch :+1: do you have any idea how to write a test for this? I still haven't been able to repro the error.
I have 0 idea how to repro. But I once suggested to ulf that we write a fuzzer to try to set skykeys to null randomly to see if the function behave correctly in all the cases.

@serynth pointed me towards https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/master/src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/analysis/BuildViewTest.java#L795 which seems to force the order of skyframe evaluation in the buildview analysis phase. Perhaps we could do something similar?
